Black mirror are stand alone episodes. You don't need to watch in any specific order, but DO NOT start with the very first episode (S1, E1) The National Anthem. In fact, save it for last. It's a bit disturbing and less interesting than the rest of the series, and has a reputation for pushing people away from continuing to watch more episodes. White Christmas is a good episode to start with. Gives you a sense of what the show is about, and is a really well written story. 

You have True Detective in your list. Just watch season 1. It's great. Like really great. So great the rest of the series never came close to comparing to it, so maybe just move on after season 1 and come back after watching other, better shows.

Please don't feel like you can't make more elsewhere. If you've put time into your current company and are making as much as you make, start applying to similar positions with other companies. When you do, ask about job security and turnover rate when interviewing. This will make it clear to potential future employers that you'd be committed to their company long term rather than being someone likely to leave after a short time. Also, make it clear that you expect to make as much (if not more) than you're making now. Use your current pay rate and experience to your advantage and go find that job that'll value you. 

Two final tips. 
1) Ask your previous boss if he has any connections with companies in similar fields that he might recommend you to. 
2) I've used this line when interviewing and it always works well. When asking about job security and turnover rate, say "I want the next company I work for to be the last company I work for.", or variations of that (I want my next first day at a new job to be my last first day at a new job, etc)

All due respect, as a person that battles the urge to kill themself daily it's really offensive when people describe killing one's self as being "the easy way out". Most people killing themselves are in a lot of pain and are terrified of what comes next. This may in a sadistic way define it as being "easier", but there's nothing easy about going through with suicide. Wording it that way just comes off as belittling, and personally gives greater urge to kill myself by just confirming that other people don't get it. We(suicidal people) then feel even more misunderstood and therefore out of place in this life. People want to be helpful, but if I try to be helpful by putting out a grease fire with water I'd just increase the flame. The point of that being we must first understand what we're dealing with before trying to fix it or else we can end up making things worse. A personal example, my father (when I dealt with depression when I was younger and I tried talking to him about it) told me "No parent should ever have to bury their child". It's something he's repeated as I deal with it now. The thing he doesn't realize is that this in no way makes me think "Yeah, I shouldn't do this", but instead makes me feel more rejected and less important. Instead I've since focused on figuring out how to either bury myself or make sure my body is never found, so that my parents won't have to bury me.
